title: About - Startup Colorado
text: THE RIGHT TO START A BUSINESS IN YOUR HOMETOWN OUR mission “ To build a sustainable statewide network of human, social, and financial capital resources supporting rural entrepreneurs, so that people and places can thrive and chart their own futures.” Startup Colorado is a 501c3 nonprofit organization that supports rural entrepreneurs and ecosystem builders in 53 rural counties across Colorado. We believe that anyone should have the ability to start and scale a business in the place they call home. We’re here to help both entrepreneurs and ecosystem builders access the human, social, and financial capital they need to build thriving businesses. Colorado’s rural communities are giving rise to some of the most exciting business opportunities in the state—from scalable tech to Main Street retail—but numerous challenges remain. The growing cost-of-living and housing crises, lack of childcare, and difficulties accessing a skilled workforce are among many of the issues rural entrepreneurs face. Our team lives in rural Colorado and understands many of these pain points firsthand. We also know that if you’ve seen one rural community, you’ve seen one rural community. That’s why we’ve logged thousands of miles getting to know our rural neighbors in-person. We develop grassroots, community-led programming that matches the unique needs of each startup community. In everything we do, our North Star is building a culture of potential for rural entrepreneurs. Press contact: margaret@startupcolorado.org for more information. title: Workforce Development Resource Hub - Startup Colorado
text: Workforce Development Resource Hub for Colorado Founders Supporting Business Owners in Job Creation Hiring is one of the biggest investments—and risks—a founder can take. Unlike large corporations, small businesses and startups don’t have extensive resources to absorb the cost of hiring, onboarding, and training employees. Yet, our State and local economies rely on business owners like you to generate jobs. In fact, startups create more jobs in their first year of operation than any other sector of the economy. At Startup Colorado, we recognize that hiring as a small business is a high-stakes decision—one that can either accelerate growth or put financial strain on a company. Payroll, benefits, training, and operational adjustments all come at a cost, and for many rural businesses, finding and retaining the right employees is an even bigger challenge. Our mission is to reduce the risk of hiring so you can: Leverage new employees to fuel growth rather than slow it down Build a strong, committed workforce behind your vision Compete with larger employers by accessing state-funded hiring and training resources Scale sustainably without being held back by workforce challenges Colorado offers a wealth of resources to help small businesses recruit, train, and retain employees while maximizing workforce incentives. This Workforce Resource Hub is designed to give founders and business owners the tools, incentives, and funding they need to hire confidently, grow faster, and strengthen their businesses—because when you succeed, so does our entire economy. title: Rural Creative Collective - Startup Colorado
text: Rural Creative Collective RURAL CREATIVE COLLECTIVE Connecting and supporting rural creatives across Colorado The Rural Creative Collective is a statewide network for artists, makers, and creative entrepreneurs living and working in rural Colorado. We connect creatives across disciplines/mediums to share resources, spark collaboration, and strengthen the cultural fabric of rural communities. Our goal is to close the gap in access to funding, community, and mentorship so rural creatives can thrive where they live and work. WHO IS A CREATIVE? At the Rural Creative Collective, we define “creatives” broadly to include individuals working across a wide spectrum of mediums, both traditional and digital. This includes visual artists such as painters, illustrators, sculptors, printmakers, photographers, and muralists; craft-based creators like ceramicists, woodworkers, fiber artists (including quilting, weaving, knitting, and embroidery), jewelry makers, glass artists, and metalworkers; Performing artists such as musicians, singers, composers, dancers, choreographers, actors, and theatre-makers. It also includes literary artists like writers, poets, playwrights, editors, and storytellers, as well as culinary creatives including chefs, bakers, and food artisans. In the digital realm, we include graphic designers, web designers, UX/UI designers, digital illustrators, animators (2D and 3D), video editors, filmmakers, content creators, podcasters, game designers, AR/VR creators, and digital marketers. Creative entrepreneurs, makers, cultural workers, arts educators, curators, event producers, and those leading community-based or socially engaged creative projects. Credit: NASA A team at the Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP) at the University of Colorado Boulder has received a $2 million award to develop a concept study for a NASA mission that will investigate how Earth’s lower atmosphere influences the upper atmosphere. The results will improve and expand our understanding of the space weather system surrounding our planet. The group, which is led by LASP researcher Aimee Merkel, is one of three selected by NASA to develop detailed proposals for the agency’s DYNAMIC (Dynamical Neutral Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling) mission. DYNAMIC will make measurements in Earth’s upper atmosphere using multiple spacecraft to enable simultaneous observations from different locations. title: Basecamps: Empower Your Communities!
text: Basecamps: Empower Your Communities! Skip to main content Close Search Basecamps Accelerating impact and connecting communities. Ashley Ranking, 2025 Environmental Sustainability Entrepreneurship Program Alumna Fellow-led, Basecamps are tailored events designed to impact the entrepreneur's local community. With a focus on individual outcomes and connections, Basecamps spark local change and deliver real value for small-business owners, local leaders, and aspiring entrepreneurs. Each Fellow receives specialized-event training, ample resources and templates, and an additional stipend to kickstart their event. Basecamp Benefits Community Engagement: Building a shared sense of purpose and local knowledge. Networking Platforms: Connecting emerging leaders with mentors, experts, and participants. Skill Building: Facilitating hands-on practice and application, as well as fostering professional growth opportunities. Our Journey of Impact 25,000 Participants Reached 340 Basecamps Hosted How It Works 1 Preparation and Planning: Receive support through meetings, brainstorming sessions, and one-on-one mentoring with the Watson Institute’s team, including in-depth guidance, resources, and a financial stipend. 2 Execute and Deliver: Run your Basecamp to engage with your local community, build connections, and grow your venture through interactive activities and sessions. 3 Celebrate and Iterate: Celebrate the outcomes of the Basecamp by leveraging connections and feedback to propel your future momentum.
